Forecasting Phone Volume with R

R
Published

July 7, 2026

Can we use R to forecast phone volume for the city of Mesa Arizona?

Breif EDA & Cleaning

Calls Offered by Service

I’m starting by looking at the number of calls offered for each service.

Code 
offer_by_q <- data |>
  group_by(`Service Name`) |>
  summarise(`Calls Offered` = sum(`Calls Offered`, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(`Calls Offered`))

Calls Offered for Each Payment Related Services

I am not sure what all the queues are, but see ‘payment’ in here. Lets focus our analysis on payment lines.

Code 
payment_data <- data |>
  filter(str_detect(`Service Name`, regex("payment", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  group_by(`Service Name`) |>
  summarise(`Calls Offered` = sum(`Calls Offered`, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(`Calls Offered`))
payment_data
# A tibble: 12 × 2
   `Service Name`                 `Calls Offered`
   <chr>                                    <dbl>
 1 - CIS_IS_MakePayment_E                  117157
 2 96 - CIS_IS_MakePayment_E               101005
 3 - CIS_IS_MakePayment_S                   13072
 4 97 - CIS_IS_MakePayment_S                 8583
 5 94 - CIS_IS_MakePaymentError_E            5733
 6 - CIS_IS_MakePaymentError_E               5118
 7 - CIS_IS_MakePaymentError_S               1334
 8 95 - CIS_IS_MakePaymentError_S            1096
 9 - CIS_IS_PaymentsOff_E                      86
10 - CIS_IS_PaymentsOff_S                      34
11 103 - CIS_IS_PaymentsOff_S                  24
12 102 - CIS_IS_PaymentsOff_E                   3

For payments, it looks like customers can call in to reach:

  • Make Payment: Caller is trying to make a payment.

  • Make Payment Error: Caller had an issue while making a payment.

  • Payments Off: Payment option may have been unavailable, and caller was routed here.

I am also going to assume the ‘E’ is for English lines and ‘S’ is for Spanish lines.

Calls Offered for All Payment Services

To somewhat simplify this analysis, lets start by looking at calls offed for all payment services as a whole.

Code 
payment_monthly <- data |>
  mutate(`Reporting Date` = as_date(parse_date_time(`Reporting Date`, orders = c("ymd", "mdy")))) |>
  filter(str_detect(`Service Name`, regex("payment", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  group_by(`Reporting Date`) |>
  summarise(`Calls Offered` = sum(`Calls Offered`, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(`Reporting Date`))

Visualize Payments by Month

Lets look at payments by month, and compare each year.

Code 
payment_monthly |>
  mutate(
    year = year(`Reporting Date`),
    month = month(`Reporting Date`, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = `Calls Offered`)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = `Calls Offered`), vjust = -0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ year, ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Payment Calls Offered by Month",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Calls Offered"
  )

Right away we can see a large range of calls between 1,502 and 6,491 since 2018. It also looks like call volume has been decreasing the last couple of years compared to pre-pandemic call volumes.

Last 5 Years Summary Stats

It looks like we are missing some data in 2021 from March - May. Lets filter out anything before June 2021 and observe the summary stats.

Code 
payment_monthly <- payment_monthly |>
  filter(`Reporting Date` >= as.Date("2021-06-01"))
summary(payment_monthly)
 Reporting Date       Calls Offered 
 Min.   :2021-06-01   Min.   :1705  
 1st Qu.:2022-09-01   1st Qu.:1981  
 Median :2023-12-01   Median :2150  
 Mean   :2023-12-01   Mean   :2168  
 3rd Qu.:2025-03-01   3rd Qu.:2360  
 Max.   :2026-06-01   Max.   :2654

Cool! It looks like over the past 5 years Meza gets about 2k calls a month related to payments with a range of about 1k calls.

Visualize Payments by Quarter

Looks by month, I am not seeing obvious consistent spikes or dips in the data so I am going to look at it by quarter to see if there if there might be any seasonal trends.

Code 
payment_quarterly <- payment_monthly |>
  mutate(
    year = year(`Reporting Date`),
    quarter = paste0("Q", quarter(`Reporting Date`))
  ) |>
  group_by(year, quarter) |>
  summarise(`Calls Offered` = sum(`Calls Offered`, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

payment_quarterly |>
  ggplot(aes(x = quarter, y = `Calls Offered`)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = `Calls Offered`), vjust = -0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ year, ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Payment Calls Offered by Quarter",
    x = "Quarter",
    y = "Calls Offered"
  )

I am not seeing any seasonal trends that are too obvious. Perhaps there is a dip in quarter three, but I will be curious to see what our forecast comes up with for the next few months (Q3) of 2026.

Prepare for Prophet

Now we need to slightly modify our data for the Prophet model. Mainly just changing the column headers.

Code 
prophet_payment <- payment_monthly |>
  transmute(
    ds = `Reporting Date`,
    y = `Calls Offered`
  ) |>
  arrange(ds)

Prophet

Code 
# model data
model_prophet <- prophet(
  prophet_payment,
  weekly.seasonality = FALSE,
  daily.seasonality = FALSE
)
# forecast the next 12 month
future <- make_future_dataframe(
  model_prophet,
  periods = 12,
  freq = "month"
)
# generate forecast
forecast <- predict(model_prophet, future)
# plot
plot(model_prophet, forecast) |>
  ggplotly()
Warning: Aspect ratios aren't yet implemented, but you can manually set a
suitable height/width
Warning: Aspect ratios aren't yet implemented, but you can manually set a
suitable height/width
Code 
# modify data
forecast_yoy <- forecast |>
  select(ds, yhat, yhat_lower, yhat_upper) |>
  left_join(prophet_payment, by = "ds") |>
  mutate(
    `Calls Offered` = if_else(is.na(y), yhat, y),
    type = if_else(is.na(y), "Forecast", "Actual"),
    year = year(ds),
    month = month(ds, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)
  )
# plot 
forecast_yoy |>
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = `Calls Offered`, fill = type)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(`Calls Offered`)), vjust = -0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ year, ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Payment Calls Offered Forecast by Month",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Calls Offered",
    fill = NULL
  )
